accepted.name: No Child Left Behind
accepted.description: A US federal education policy that paired annual testing, subgroup reporting and accountability consequences. Its evidence record includes reported math gains, weaker reading effects and implementation incentives that can affect interpretation.

accepted.name: Head Start
accepted.description: A US federal early-childhood program serving children from low-income families. The linked study evaluates access against the care arrangements available to its control group.

accepted.name: Chicago double-dose algebra
accepted.description: A Chicago Public Schools ninth-grade policy that paired algebra with an additional support period for students below a prior-math-score threshold. Its effects depend on assignment, instructional time and classroom organization.

accepted.name: Early Warning Intervention and Monitoring System (EWIMS)
accepted.description: A seven-step early-warning process that uses attendance, behavior and course-performance data to identify students, assign supports and monitor progress. The linked trial evaluates one first-year implementation, not every local data tool.

accepted.name: Comprehensive teacher induction
accepted.description: An induction model using trained full-time mentors, instructional support, professional development, observation, and feedback for beginning teachers. The study distinguishes one- and two-year district implementations.

review.reason: Published secondary-math evaluation scope is narrower than original alternate-route umbrella
